image_description: A close-up, side-profile view of a large crocodile resting on a rocky surface. The head is positioned to the left with the mouth slightly open, revealing teeth. The body extends to the right, displaying heavy, textured armor plating (scutes). The lighting highlights the rough texture of the skin and the stone foreground.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The snout tapers distinctly towards the nose, forming a clear 'V' shape characteristic of crocodiles rather than the 'U' shape of alligators. The profile is clearly visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is partially open, not closed. While teeth are visible, the specific condition of 'interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed' (specifically the 4th lower tooth fitting into a socket) cannot be verified in this state. Furthermore, the teeth appear somewhat uniform and lack the distinct size variation and sharp definition expected in a high-fidelity biological render; they look slightly fused or soft.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The eye is visible but appears as a dark, indistinct blob. There is no resolution to see a vertical slit pupil or a nictitating membrane. The eye lacks the glossy, wet reflection typical of a living reptile eye, appearing more like a painted detail.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Two distinct nostril openings are visible at the very end of the snout, consistent with crocodilian anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body shows significant bulk and is covered in thick, raised scales indicating heavy armor.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal surface exhibits a chaotic but generally row-like arrangement of large, bony plates (scutes), matching the description of osteoderms.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coloration is predominantly yellowish-green/olive, not the 'dark brown to grey' specified in the checkpoint. While the texture is rough, the color mismatch is significant for a strict verification.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The crocodile is lying on its belly/side on a rock; the ventral (belly) surface is completely occluded by the body itself and the ground.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: No limbs or feet are visible in the frame; the body is tucked against the rock.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is not visible in the frame; only the head and anterior trunk are shown.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The teeth lack individual definition and sharp edges; they appear to melt into the gum line and each other, resembling a continuous serrated ridge rather than distinct conical structures. This is a common AI artifact in rendering complex repetitive biological structures.

The eye lacks anatomical depth and specular highlights. It appears as a flat, dark smudge on the side of the head rather than a spherical organ set within a socket, suggesting a failure to render complex organic geometry.

The connection between the lower jaw and the skull (quadrate bone area) looks anatomically vague. The lower jaw seems to taper off without a clear hinge mechanism, blending slightly into the neck scales.
